text:
mira: Heads up — seeing a sustained p95 latency jump on /api/generate for enterprise-tier. Baseline ~220ms, now ~480ms during a 30m window.

tyler: Any recent commits to the kernel selector or batching logic? saw a change last night.

mira: Yep, merged a kernel-selection tweak that prefers fused-attn kernels on A100s for throughput. Rollout started 4h ago. Also noticed more microbatches of size 1-2 in the profiler.

caroline: Do you have the flamegraph or kv cache stats?

mira: Pasting short profiler excerpt + kv stats:

```
# microbatch size distribution (last 30m):
size=1 -> 42%
size=2 -> 31%
size=4 -> 15%
size>=8 -> 12%

KV cache hit ratio (enterprise route):
avg hit=68% (prev ~88%)
median latency per token (server-side): 1.9ms -> 3.6ms
```

alex: Interesting — fused kernels optimize compute but they can change token alignment and scheduling, causing more prefix flushes and worse KV locality. Combined with static token budgets per route, batches are forming suboptimally.

tyler: If batches are landing as lots of small microbatches, per-token overhead and kernel setup time blow up p95. We should check queue policy: are we dispatching on token_budget or on time window? current config uses token_budget=256 static per route.

mira: Exactly. My hypothesis: kernel selection change altered per-request token emission pattern -> more small responses -> static token_budget causes immediate dispatch instead of waiting to accumulate better microbatches. Result: lower KV efficiency and higher p95.

caroline: Two levers to try: 1) make token_budget dynamic by route/tier based on SLO (p95 target) and observed queue depth; 2) fallback kernel selector for short sequences (force non-fused for seq_len < 32).

alex: Proposed dynamic token_budget formula (sketch):

```
# token_budget = clamp(base * (target_p95 / observed_p95) * tier_weight, min=32, max=1024)
# tier_weight: enterprise=1.2, standard=1.0, free=0.8
```

tyler: That looks reasonable as a heuristic. Need to be careful with feedback loops — if observed_p95 spikes, budget increases which might increase latency further. Add smoothing over 5-minute EWMA and a cooldown window.

mira: Agreed. Also throttle changes so they only apply if queue_length > X (to avoid changing for already-small bursts).

infra-bot: canary deploy started for config changes (id: canary-2026-03-17-01)

caroline: For the kernel fallback tweak I suggest a conservative rule: if seq_len <= 32 and kv_hit_ratio < 80% for route then prefer non-fused kernel for next N requests. Helps keep KV locality.

tyler: We should also update microbatch allocator: it picks microbatch_count based on token_budget. If token_budget changes dynamically we need to ensure allocator doesn't thrash GPU occupancy. Add hysteresis.

mira: Plan: run an A/B on the enterprise route on a dedicated canary pool. Two variants:
A) dynamic token_budget + EWMA smoothing + allocator hysteresis
B) kernel fallback thresholds for short seqs + kv-based gating
Measure p95, kv_hit_ratio, throughput for 2 hours.

alex: I'll add the experiment config to launchpad and a tiny load harness to replay real request len distribution. link: https://launchpad.internal/exp/584

caroline: I'll wire up a dashboard: p95, p50, kv_hit, microbatch_dist, kernels_used, batch_wait_ms. Add alerts if p95 > 400ms for >5m.

evals-bot: added regression suite 'short-chat' -> will run on canary and notify on diffs.

tyler: One more thing: watch tail latencies on other routes — dynamic token budgeting might steal capacity if routing uses shared GPUs. Ensure smart routing policy still honors tier isolation.

mira: Good call. In canary we keep enterprise pinned to its own GPU pool to isolate effects.

caroline: rollout plan: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% if no regressions. Each step min 30m observation.

mira: I'll run experiment tomorrow 02:00 PST. Will post initial results in this thread once available. Thanks all.

alex: :thumbsup:

tyler: SGTM

mira: Closing thread for now — follow-ups will be added after the run (will include flamegraphs and kv heatmaps).
